abstract: Metasurfaces are increasingly employed for sophisticated polarization transformations, including general unitary and nonunitary Jones operations. Despite substantial advances in analytical synthesis methods, inverse design of these transformations remains challenging. Here, we show that the particular mathematical structure of Jones polarization transformations makes optimal effective-susceptibility synthesis analytically tractable within the generalized sheet transition condition (GSTC) framework. For reciprocal, lossless dipolar metasurfaces, we establish exact feasibility and global minimum attainment, and derive sharp effective-susceptibility bounds for representative unitary and nonunitary transformations. We identify when magnetoelectric coupling lowers the minimum susceptibility, when it offers no resource advantage, and how the required material response depends on the prescribed polarization transformation. Applications to polarization rotations, tunable compensators, and polarization-state separation, including unambiguous discrimination, demonstrate sharp physical limits and material-resource trade-offs. These results provide geometry-independent theoretical benchmarks that can guide numerical inverse design and the selection of metasurface architectures.
